    Mission 01 · The Haunted Archetype_□×
    FileEditViewHelp

    A Halloween tarot quiz. Eight questions deal you one of six spirits, and tell you how that spirit uses AI.

    Role
    Concept, questions, scoring and design. ChatGPT and Claude for prototyping and build.
    Format
    Browser quiz, 8 questions, about 2 minutes
    Tools
    HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, hand-drawn SVG sigils, Web Audio API
    Team
    Solo
    Timeline
    About a week
    Reach
    Posted in three internal groups at work, seen by 15,329, 739 and 194 people
    Evidence
    30+ replies and 50+ reactions in the threads. No analytics, by design.
    Data
    Nothing you answer is stored or sent
    ▶ Play itGitHub

    Watch it

    Screenshots

    What you get

    • A tarot cardDealt with your spirit's sigil and a one-line tagline that is a little too accurate.
    • A reading and three strengthsThe version of you that shows up when the lights cut out.
    • Your AI ritualHow your spirit actually uses AI. People sent theirs to coworkers.
    • A copy buttonDrop your result in the group chat and make everyone else take it.

    Design choices I would defend

    • Same answers, same card, every time.Ties never break randomly. A fixed order decides, so friends can compare results and trust them.
    • Sound is off until you turn it on.The wind, slow chords and little bells are generated live in the browser. No audio files.
    • Nothing is stored.Not a single answer leaves the page. It is a game, not a data grab.

    Cheat codes

    Two small pieces of the real code. The rest stays in the deck.

    // every answer feeds two spirits
const [, p, s] = QUESTIONS[qi].o[ai];
pts[p] += 2; prim[p] += 1; pts[s] += 1;

// ties never break randomly
const TIEBREAK = ["F","M","P","W","O","S"];
    // ambience chords: Am7 Fmaj7 G Em7
const CHORDS = [[45,57,60,64,67],[41,53,57,60,64],[43,55,59,62,67],[40,52,55,59,64]];

    What happened

    15,329people saw the post in the largest group. The other two groups saw it at 739 and 194.
    30+replies across the threads, plus more than 50 reactions on the posts.
    6 of 6spirits showed up in the replies. People kept posting which one they got.

    I shared it in internal AI and women-in-tech groups over two weeks in October. People posted their cards in the format the quiz gives them, ended with "Which one are you?", and sent it to their teams. Two people asked Copilot to paint a portrait of their spirit. Three people reached out afterward: two LinkedIn connections and one direct message.

    What people said

    Names are left out. These are short lines from the threads, and one thread with the names blurred.

    ✔ What this shows

    • I can take a concept from rules to a finished, shareable experience on my own.
    • I design for sharing: the result is built to be pasted into a chat.
    • I can build interactive sound and visuals with no libraries.

    ✘ What this does not show

    • That the archetypes are valid. They are playful fiction, not a psychological assessment.
    • How many people played. The view counts are post views, not quiz plays, and I store no data.
    • A neutral sample. People who replied chose to, and they are mostly coworkers.

    What I learned

    People passed it around because the result felt like theirs. The card is what travelled, more than the eight questions, so I would spend the next round of effort on the result screen.

    What I would change

    I would add a simple way to count how many people finish it, without storing anyone's answers. Right now I only know what people chose to tell me in the replies.

    Done
    Mission 02 · Bandz on Shuffle_□×
    FileEditViewHelp

    A rhythm game on an iPod click wheel. You catch Silly Bandz on the beat, and every catch plays the next note of the song.

    Role
    Game design, interaction design, sound design and front-end. ChatGPT and Claude for prototyping and build.
    Format
    Browser rhythm game with an iPod-style menu
    Tools
    HTML, CSS, JavaScript, canvas and the Web Audio API. Sound is synthesized, no audio files.
    Team
    Solo
    Timeline
    About a week
    Reach
    A bunch of coworkers
    Evidence
    Coworkers played it. I did not collect formal feedback.
    Saves
    Keeps your bandz collection in your browser
    ▶ Play itGitHub

    Watch it

    Screenshots

    How it plays

    • You don't pick. It picks.Shuffle plays a random track at a random remix speed, with bandz coming from anywhere on the wheel, like an iPod Shuffle.
    • Catch on the beat.Each catch plays the next note of the song, builds your combo and earns timing calls like Perfect.
    • Fill the glow meter.The meter fills with rainbow, and your bandz light up in the dark.
    • Keep your wrist.Every band you catch goes into a collection, with a running total.

    The details

    The tracks are named like 2009 memories: Recess, Bus Ride Home, Top 8. There are nine iPod colors to pick from, and a No Sound setting.

    Why a click wheel

    For me, 2009 was school: Silly Bandz on everyone's wrists, iPod Nanos, iPod Shuffles, and the first iPad in the news. I had an iPod Nano. While other kids had cell phones, I played games on mine, listened to music and watched music videos. The click wheel felt ahead of its time, and it is the part of that year that is most me. I wanted anyone who was a kid then to feel it again in one tap.

    A hard part I solved

    Making a catch feel good on the beat. Each catch has to play the next note of the song, grade your timing and keep the combo going, with sound I synthesize live. I tuned the timing windows by playing it over and over until a Perfect felt earned and a near miss still felt fair.

    ✔ What this shows

    • I can design the feel of a game: timing, sound and feedback.
    • I can synthesize sound in the browser with no audio files.
    • I sweat small details, down to the track names.

    ✘ What this does not show

    • That players enjoyed it. I did not collect formal feedback.
    • How well the timing works on every device, from phones to trackpads.
    • Replay value. I do not know how long anyone kept playing.

    Cheat codes

    Three small pieces of the real code. The rest stays in the deck.

    // how close to the beat marker counts as a catch
if (d <= sp*0.45)   { n.res = "perfect"; hit(n, 100, "PERFECT"); }
else if (d <= sp+2) { n.res = "nice";    hit(n, 50,  "NICE");    }
else                { n.res = "miss"; game.combo = 0; }

// the glow meter charges faster on perfect catches
game.charge += pts === 100 ? 1.25 : 1;
if (game.charge >= GLOW_AT) game.ready = true;

// every catch plays the next note of the hook
lead(n.m, ac.currentTime, n.harmony ? 0.07 : 0.13);

    What I learned

    Timing windows decide whether a rhythm game feels fair. I kept adjusting until a miss felt like my own mistake and not the game's, and I would test that with people who have never played one.

    What I would change

    I would add a share card for your bandz collection, the way the quiz has a result you can paste into a chat. A game people send to friends needs something to send.

    Mission 03 · The Clarity Arcade_□×
    FileEditViewHelp

    Six short games made for AfroTech attendees, about confusing words, sketchy job posts and the kind of conference person you really are.

    Role
    Concept, writing, design and build. ChatGPT and Claude for prototyping and build.
    Format
    Six browser games, 30 seconds to 2 minutes each
    Tools
    HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Web Audio API. All sound is generated live in the browser.
    Team
    Solo
    Timeline
    About a week
    Reach
    Shared on LinkedIn for AfroTech attendees. Around 20 people played.
    Evidence
    A couple of people in the AfroTech community said they appreciated it.
    Look
    Black and green, with a Pan-African pattern strip
    ▶ Play it

    Watch it

    Screenshots

    The six games

    • Jargon Jail8 rounds of translating corporate and health speak into plain English.
    • Fix This App60 seconds to spot everything wrong with a terrible cookout RSVP app.
    • Your AfroTech Archetype6 questions, then a mission to go find your match at the conference.
    • Red Flag or Green Flag10 swipes on job posts and recruiter DMs. Run or apply?
    • Follow-Up Note MakerA LinkedIn note after a good chat, in a few taps.
    • Afro MixerMix Afrobeats, Amapiano and Afro House. Get the crowd moving.

    The Afro Mixer

    You pick a genre, press play and stack up to seven layers: drums, rim clave, shaker, bass, dreamy keys, kalimba and talking drum. Each pad shows that instrument's frequencies live, and a crowd of little figures reacts as the energy climbs. Nine missions earn you a DJ title, starting at Aux Cord Apprentice. Every instrument is tuned so the home note, C, rings at 528 Hz, and every sound is generated in the browser.

    The idea

    The line on the home page says it: good design helps people feel less lost, and these games are a small, silly way to practice spotting the difference. Conferences hand first-timers a lot of guides and schedules. A quick game is a friendlier way in: it is fun, it is interactive, and it gets people talking about how to read the room before they walk it.

    ✔ What this shows

    • I can design a whole set of games for one audience and one look.
    • I can write for a specific community, with its music, jokes and job-hunt pain.
    • I build sound and live visuals in the browser with no audio files.

    ✘ What this does not show

    • Impact at the event. I did not attend, so I shared it online for attendees.
    • That the games taught anyone anything. They are playful practice.
    • Scale. Around 20 people played, so this is an early signal.

    What I learned

    A conference game works when it asks for a minute and no sign-up. Every screen between the tap and the first fun moment is a place someone walks away, so I kept cutting them.

    What I would change

    I would add a daily challenge and a leaderboard, so attendees at the event could play against each other and compare scores in the hallway.

    Mission 04 · The Haunted Headset_□×
    FileEditViewHelp

    A Halloween game for call center and customer service reps. Eight phone calls, one possessed script, and a cryptid waiting at the end of their shift.

    Role
    Concept, writing, cover art, direction and design. ChatGPT and Claude for prototyping and build.
    Format
    Browser mini game: a shift simulation with eight calls, a result card, a DJ mixer and a bingo card
    Tools
    HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, Web Audio API
    Team
    Solo
    Made for
    Call center and customer service reps, Halloween 2026
    Data
    Every caller is fictional. No real data, and it is entertainment, not training.
    ▶ Play itGitHub

    Watch it

    Screenshots

    The idea

    I understand the work that call center and customer service reps do, so I turned a shift into a short simulation they can play. The calls are fictional, the situations are familiar, and the script is possessed.

    What you get

    • Eight callsEach one is a short scene with four ways to handle it. The script is possessed, so the choices get stranger as the shift goes on.
    • Three metersSanity, Adherence and Hold Time move with every choice. You watch them while you decide.
    • A cryptid and a Soul ScoreSurvive the shift and you get a character, a dark gift, a survival strategy and a prophecy for your next one.
    • A DJ mixerPick a pad for each layer of a haunted beat, then drop the mix to get a remix of your call you can copy and share. It is modeled on the mixer from my first product.
    • Haunted Call BingoA bingo card for the moments everyone on the floor knows.

    What I learned

    Specific jokes travel. Every call starts from a moment people on the floor already recognize, so the scenes got a laugh before any score appeared.

    What I would change

    I would show how the three meters add up to the Soul Score. Right now you see the numbers and the result, but not the math between them.

    Hi, I'm Olu.

    I make interactive things for people who like to play. I write the concept and the rules, build a working version fast, and see what happens when real people try it.

    Background
    Computer science at UNC Charlotte with a concentration in AI, robotics and gaming. Coursework in human-computer interaction, cyberpsychology, product, UI and UX design, e-commerce and business. Google UX credentials.
    How I build
    Solo, in vanilla JavaScript, CSS and SVG, with the Web Audio API for sound. I use AI tools to prototype and build, and I write down what that looked like in each case.
    What I care about
    Experiences that make people curious enough to try them, and honest enough to say what they do not prove.
    Also
    I design health and wellness experiences too. See my health portfolio and my original portfolio.
    Next
    Applying to HCI master's programs for 2027, and looking for creative technologist and prototyping roles.

    How I use AI

    What I bring
    The idea, the rules, the tone and what the player should feel. I decide what the game is before any tool gets involved.
    What the tools do
    ChatGPT and Claude help me prototype and build. They draft code and options quickly, and I choose, rewrite and reject. With a computer science degree, I read what comes back and change it myself.
    Where I check
    I play every build myself, then put it in front of real people. Timing, wording and fairness get judged by playing, not by trusting a draft.
    What it buys me
    The first three projects each took about a week, start to finish.
